P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, through a local bank or financial institution. Under the Foreign Exchange Regulations 2022, a resident entitled to a payment from a non-resident must receive it through a bank or financial institution. Residents may hold any amount of foreign currency and keep FX accounts locally. No surrender requirement was found. Residents may NOT keep bank accounts abroad without the Governor's approval. Since 2025 (Foreign Currency Use Regulations, GN 198/2025), DOMESTIC prices and payments must be in TZS. Cross-border transactions with a genuinely foreign counterparty may stay in foreign currency.

sources.title: These New Regulations Seek to Control Dollar Trade in Tanzania (20 May 2022)
sources.quote: Additionally, a person resident in the country who has a right to receive a payment from a person resident outside the United Republic must receive such payment through a bank or financial institution.

sources.quote: The FX Regulations 2022 continue to restrict residents from opening and maintaining foreign bank accounts without the approval of the Governor of the BoT.

sources.title: Tanzania Foreign Currency Regulations 2025: What Businesses Must Know About The TZS Mandate
sources.quote: Foreign loans from international lenders, cross-border transactions between a Tanzanian party and a genuinely foreign counterparty, and certain international trade arrangements retain the ability to use foreign currency.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: The BoT texts (FX Regulations 2022; GN 198/2025) were not read directly; three law-firm/press summaries agree. A 'foreign' platform paying a Tanzanian freelancer is cross-border; domestic clients must be invoiced in TZS.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. The FX Regulations 2022 let residents and non-residents open and keep a foreign-currency account with a bank or financial institution in Tanzania. Accounts abroad need BoT Governor approval, with narrow exceptions.

P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for United Republic of Tanzania (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration); YouTube Partner Program. Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: Newly yes, via M-Pesa. Vodacom M-Pesa Tanzania and PayPal announced an integration on 26 May 2026. Eligible M-Pesa customers can link their PayPal account in the M-Pesa Super App, deposit into PayPal and withdraw PayPal balances back to M-Pesa. Vodacom said limits, full eligibility and go-live timelines would follow through its channels. Before this, Tanzanians had to route PayPal funds through Payoneer, virtual cards or Kenyan accounts. Tanzania is not on the PayPal Payouts list.

P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: available. Tanzanian users can receive from clients and marketplaces and withdraw to local bank accounts. Wise: Tanzania is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money, though a 2026 developer guide tells Tanzanians to open Wise USD accounts. Sending money TO Tanzania via Wise is a different service.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A person who becomes potentially liable to tax by carrying on a business must apply for a TIN within 15 days of starting. After a TRA assessment interview and tax clearance, they get a Business Licence from the district/municipal/city trade office or the Ministry of Industry and Trade, depending on the business type. Business names are registered with BRELA (not researched in detail). Simplest form: a sole proprietor under the presumptive regime (L3).

sources.quote: For business TIN purposes, a person who becomes potentially liable to tax by reason of carrying a business shall apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number within fifteen days from the date of commencing the business.

sources.quote: After fulfilling the tax obligations, the taxpayer will receive a Tax Clearance in order to acquire Business License from the Trade office in District or Municipal or City or the Ministry of Industry and Trade depending on the type of business.

L1_registration.notes: BRELA business-name rules (and whether a sole trader under own name must register) and the Business Licensing Act were not read.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The TIN from the Tanzania Revenue Authority, applied for online through the TRA taxpayer portal (taxpayerportal.tra.go.tz). Residents and non-residents can apply for a business or non-business TIN using a National Identification Number (NIN) or another valid ID (passport, driving licence, voter's ID, Zanzibar ID). Issue can take as little as 24 hours.

sources.title: Starting Business — TIN
sources.quote: The individual will need to fill out the Online TIN application form available at https://taxpayerportal.tra.go.tz and will receive instructions on how to answer the online questions and upload the necessary documents.

sources.title: Tanzania Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) - All You Need To Know
sources.quote: The taxpayer portal allows for both resident and non-resident persons to apply for either a business TIN or non-business TIN using a National Identification Number (NIN) or any valid identification card including a passport, driving license, Voters’ ID, and Zanzibar ID.

L2_tax_id.notes: Fee status of TIN registration not confirmed.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (other than short-term residents) are taxed on worldwide income. Residence tests include 183+ days in the year. The resident scale (monthly) is 0% to TZS 270,000, then 8%, 20%, 25%, and 30% above TZS 1,000,000, unchanged by Finance Act 2026. Presumptive regime for resident individuals: from 1 July 2026 (Finance Act 2026) the turnover ceiling is TZS 200m (was 100m), at 4% of turnover for TZS 11m–200m (was 3.5%). Independent professionals and providers of technical, management, construction and training services have been excluded since 2022.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Mainland VAT is 18% (a 16% reduced rate exists for specified B2C electronic payments; Zanzibar is 15%). Registration is mandatory at TZS 200m turnover in 12 months (or TZS 100m in 6 months). Licensed professional service providers must register regardless of turnover. Exports of goods and certain services are zero-rated, including services used or enjoyed outside the United Republic (VAT Act ss.62/64).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and its 2023 Regulations. Data controllers and processors, defined to include natural persons, must register with the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) before collecting or processing personal data. The fee depends on headcount, and certificates last five years. Failing to register carries a fine of TZS 100,000 to TZS 5m. The final registration deadline was 30 April 2025.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Electronic Transactions Act 2015. A consumer may cancel within 7 days (or a longer agreed period) after receiving goods or concluding the agreement, if they have not received a material benefit (s.30). Refunds are due within 30 days. If the supplier breaches its information/order duties (s.28), the consumer may cancel within 14 days of receiving the goods or services. Orders must be executed within 30 days unless agreed otherwise (s.29).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) A new one-year presumptive tax holiday (Finance Act 2026): individuals starting a business for the first time with projected turnover of TZS 4m–200m pay nil tax for the first year from TIN issue, subject to Commissioner General approval. They must stay in the presumptive regime throughout the relief. (2) Presumptive tax of 4% up to TZS 200m (L3; professionals excluded). (3) Exported services are zero-rated (L4). (4) PayPal-to-M-Pesa withdrawals since mid-2026 (P4).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
